policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders a singular abstract noun, "And I will declare thy greatness", matching the qere singular construct וגדולתך; the ketiv וגדולתיך is plural. The same verse shows ASV marking the distinction, rendering the plural נוראתיך as "thy terrible acts" rather than an abstract singular, so the singular "greatness" here reflects the qere and not a collapsed plural.
